text: RL Triage Agent investigates robot learning failures. It connects model hypotheses to inspections, registered repairs, and behavioral tests.
First, a freshly captured normal policy in Isaac Lab. This is a simulated Go two robot, following a motion command on Nebius L forty S compute.
With the known F one reward defect, the robot barely follows that command. These are normal and faulty captures, not a before and after repair video.

Now the application replays a separate, completed P P O epoch failure. The public source files are hash verified. Both policies survive twenty seconds, but linear tracking error rises from zero point one four six to one point one six nine meters per second.

The recorded Nemotron response first selects the reward inspection. It returns normal. The following inspections use the registered sequence, rather than more model choices. This matters: a plausible first hypothesis is not a confirmed mechanism.

A short optimizer inspection finds the discrepancy. Five epochs and four minibatches should produce twenty optimizer steps per update. The faulty configuration produces only four. These are fresh three update inspections, not measurements loaded from the trained checkpoint.

The registered correction restores the configured epoch count. The recorded approval chain is proposed, approved, consumed, then receipt. Training restarts with a different seed. This replay reads those artifacts; it does not issue a new approval or run training.

Recovery is tested separately across twenty six fixed conditions. The corrected policy's linear tracking error is zero point one four eight meters per second, near the normal control. Its checkpoint hash and evaluation metrics match the recorded summary.

A separate compound defect needs another loop. In two development seeds, the first correction is insufficient. Both pass after the second correction, in opposite orders. These are known defect development results, not evidence of unseen fault generalization or model superiority.

Simulation uses Brev provisioned Nebius L forty S compute. Nemotron inference uses NVIDIA's hosted endpoint. Token Factory calls are not yet demonstrated. Issued promotional credits are not a verified redeemed balance.
The open source package includes an English replay, source hashes, and a C P U verifier. Inspect the evidence, test the mechanism, and evaluate the repair.
